itemListElement.name: Gojo vs Karabiner-Elements: MacBook notch utility or keyboard remapper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only in the broad sense that both improve a Mac workflow. Karabiner-Elements is a keyboard customizer, while Gojo is a notch utility.
Its Simple Modifications interface can change one key to another on a selected device. Its advanced rules can define behavior for keys, consumer keys, and pointing buttons.

mainEntity.name: Does Karabiner-Elements support complex keyboard rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Its official reference documents conditional rules, including behavior based on the frontmost application, device, keyboard type, input source, variables, and expressions.

mainEntity.name: Should I install Gojo and Karabiner-Elements together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when you need both roles: Karabiner-Elements for keyboard customization and Gojo for notch-based controls and everyday Mac utilities.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose Karabiner-Elements when the problem is your keyboard: remapping a key, adapting an external keyboard, or applying detailed conditional rules. Choose Gojo when the problem is fast access to MacBook utilities through the notch, such as media, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, display, and window controls.
points: Best specialist fit: low-level keyboard remapping, external-keyboard fixes, and conditional key rules.
Best Gojo fit: notch-based controls for everyday MacBook workflows.
These tools solve different layers: keyboard events versus visible control access.

content.s: Karabiner-Elements is stronger when keyboard behavior is the product. It is purpose-built for remapping keys, importing rules, and writing conditional keyboard modifications.
Gojo is stronger when the problem is access to everyday tools. It keeps media, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, display, and window controls near the notch.

Use Karabiner-Elements for keyboard behavior, especially with external keyboards or conditional mappings, and use Gojo for notch-based daily tools. They are complementary rather than overlapping choices.

Comparison pages are only useful if they are honest about scope. Gojo is a MacBook notch utility, not a blanket replacement for every specialist app. Before granting macOS Accessibility, Automation, Camera, Calendar, or other permissions to any utility, check whether the requested access matches the feature you plan to use.
